_meta.note: UnityEngine.UI.Text is m_Script fileID 708705254 in the UnityEngine.UI assembly (guid f5f67c52d1564df4a8936ccd202a3bd8). Strings are read from the raw bytes by tools/extract/ui-text.mjs, which folds multi-line YAML scalars properly; the shared unity_yaml.js parser returns only the first line of one.

briefing.note: panel_mission carries its own disableAfterDelay: disableDelay 3.8, enabled, targeting itself, at PlayerShip_SR14_Photon.prefab:10176 and :12320, mechanism in disableAfterDelay.cs:8-16. disableDelay is a public float with NO initialiser, so 3.8 is shipped behaviour and not a code default. A panel live at spawn (see liveAtSpawn above) is therefore killed 3.8 s after spawn; one that is not does not start its countdown until something activates it, because Start() does not run on an inactive GameObject. What activates it, if anything, is NOT traced here. HUD_Ship.DelayedStart (HUD_Ship.cs:88-99) then hides it a SECOND time at 0.12+4=4.12 s, against a panel already inactive for 0.32 s. 4.12 is real but it is NOT the figure: DEV-200 made that trade on the strength of a citation pointing at HUD_Ship.cs rather than at the prefab, and DEV-217 undid it. Ends in a newline, which is in the shipped bytes.

steps.title: THE CANYON
steps.say: This is the canyon proper. Hold {throttle} and follow me in. Stay between the walls.

steps.title: A HARD CORNER
steps.say: Tap {slow} early, roll onto your side and pull round with me. Through ring {nextRing}.

steps.title: ONE, THEN THE OTHER
steps.say: Two turns back to back. Roll, pull, and roll level between them.

steps.title: THE HAIRPIN
steps.say: The tightest turn in the canyon. Slow right down with {slow}, then roll and pull hard.

steps.title: OPEN IT UP
steps.say: A straight between the walls. Hold {boost} with {throttle} and get past {target}. SPEED {speed}

steps.title: THE LAST HARD TURNS
steps.say: Let go of {boost} and tap {slow}. Two more hard turns, then we're out.

steps.title: RACE ME OUT
steps.say: Out of the canyon. Race me to the finish!

interrupts.say: Too hard. You're back on the line with a cold engine. Hold {throttle} and find me.
You hit the wall. The ship turns slowly for a moment. Climb away.
Turn back to ring {nextRing}. I'll wait.

_meta.note: Anniversary content, not 2016's. The canyon run starts in the air, at rest, so `stopped` waits six seconds rather than lesson 1's three: the first plate is read hovering, and a prompt that interrupts it to say the same thing is noise. And `lost` is 250 m off the line, not 150: this course's finish sits 178 m off its own racing line (the line bends away past the last ring), and its hairpin legs cut up to 124 m inside it, so at 150 a student flying straight at the next gate reads as lost; tests/unit/lesson-canyon.test.ts holds every lesson's threshold above its own course's chords. Every number is a first guess of the kind a playtest settles.

copiedFrom.why: 2016's EXTRACTED facts about Mesa Canyon and the course this lesson flies half of: copied rather than typed (hard rule 3), and tests/unit/lesson-canyon.test.ts deep-equals each against the generated file.

turnIndicators.rule: the indicators whose nearest ring (by the ring pos) is one of the kept rings

slicedFrom.why: adv_01_hoverJet's second half is the canyon proper (FLIGHT-INSTRUCTOR §2.6: from its ring 10 the line runs between walls for eight legs, with the course's hardest turns). Every kept ring deep-equals the source ring of the same name, the line is a contiguous slice of the source's to its end, and each indicator deep-equals the source's of the same name: tests/unit/lesson-canyon.test.ts holds all three.

geometry.frame: THREE space in the fields above; derived in sim space on the source line
geometry.note: The spawn and the respawn are DERIVED, not placed: the point 250 m of line short of adv_01_hoverJet's ring 10, at the line's height, nose level along the line's heading there (a HoverJet with no lift is let go at rest, gravity off, so it hovers). launchKind "direct" and no spawn.launch, as the glider (DEV-145): there is no elevator in the canyon. The test re-derives the point from the source line.
